did_you_know.text: Did you know? The gathering of Israel at Mizpah is described as the people assembling “as one man,” from all across the land—from Dan to Beersheba—and even from the land of Gilead.

Did you know? Before the war, Israel numbered four hundred thousand men who drew the sword, while the men of Benjamin came out with twenty-six thousand warriors, in addition to seven hundred men from Gibeah.

Did you know? In his testimony, the Levite said that the men of Gibeah had intended to kill him, but instead attacked his concubine, who died; afterward, he dismembered her and sent the pieces throughout the territory of Israel.
Did you know? Israel made a joint decision that no one would return home, but that they would act together against Gibeah and cast lots to organize the supplies and the military campaign.
Did you know? Seven hundred men of Benjamin are described as left-handed, and each one could sling a stone at a hair’s breadth without missing.
Did you know? Although Israel greatly outnumbered Benjamin, they asked the Lord who should go first into battle, and the answer was: Judah first.
Did you know? In the first battle, the men of Benjamin came out from Gibeah and struck down twenty-two thousand Israelites, despite Israel’s numerical advantage.
Did you know? On the second day, the Israelites were defeated again, and the men of Benjamin struck down another eighteen thousand men—all of them swordsmen.

Did you know? After the two defeats, Israel did not treat the matter as merely a military issue: they wept before the Lord, fasted until evening, and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings at Bethel.
Did you know? The chapter notes that in those days the ark of the covenant of God was at Bethel, and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, stood before it and inquired of the Lord during the crisis.
